title: Score Sheet With Undo
statement:
A referee keeps a score sheet. It starts empty and the referee reads out a list of entries ops, one at a time:

  • An integer, such as "7" or "-3": write that score on the sheet.
  • "+": write a new score equal to the sum of the last two scores still on the sheet.
  • "x2": write a new score equal to twice the last score on the sheet.
  • "undo": cross out the last score on the sheet. It no longer counts for anything, including later "+" and "x2".

Return the sum of all scores left on the sheet at the end. The input is always valid: "+" only appears when at least two scores are on the sheet, and "x2" and "undo" only when at least one is.

examples.why: The sheet goes 4, 7, 11, 22. "undo" removes the 22, then -3 is added: 4 + 7 + 11 − 3 = 19.
The 5 is crossed out before anything uses it. x2 doubles the 2, not the 5.
After the undo the last two scores are 1 and 2 again, so the second "+" writes 3: total 1 + 2 + 3.

constraints: every score written and the final sum have absolute value at most 10^12
hints: Every operation only looks at the most recent scores. Which structure gives cheap access to the end of a list?
Keep the scores in a stack. "undo" is a pop; "+" and "x2" read the top one or two and push.
Sum the stack at the end, or keep a running total that you update on every push and pop.

explain.intuition:
Every rule talks about "the last score" or "the last two scores", and "undo" removes the last one. That is exactly last-in, first-out, so the sheet is a stack. It works like an editor's undo history: undoing restores the previous state, and the next action builds on that state, not on what was undone.

Pushing and popping are O(1), so the whole sheet is processed in one pass. You can sum at the end or keep a running total: add on every push, subtract on every pop.
steps: For "+", push the sum of the top two. For "x2", push twice the top. For "undo", pop.
Otherwise parse the entry as an integer and push it.
Return the sum of the stack.
pitfalls: Making "+" replace the last two scores instead of adding a new one. The two scores it reads stay on the sheet.
Keeping only a running total and the last two values. After an "undo" you need the score before those, so the whole stack is required.
Parsing every entry with parseInt before checking for the commands. parseInt("x2") is NaN, and in Python int("+") raises.

solutions.title: Stack, sum at the end
solutions.idea: Model the sheet as a stack; each entry is a push or a pop.

solutions.title: Stack with a running total
solutions.idea: Same stack, but adjust the total on every push and pop so no final pass is needed.

followups: Add a "redo" entry that restores the most recently crossed-out score. What extra structure do you need, and when must it be cleared?
The referee also asks for the current total after every entry. Which solution handles that without extra cost?
